behavioral_notes.element: hr.employee._compute_exceptional_location_id + _get_current_day_location_field (how the displayed work location is resolved)
behavioral_notes.observation: The module models a remote-work schedule as two layers metadata cannot show. The recurring layer is 7 plain Many2one fields on hr.employee (monday_location_id..sunday_location_id, the DAYS list in models/hr_homeworking.py); the override layer is the hr.employee.location table (one row per employee per date, enforced by the unique(employee_id,date) Constraint). _get_current_day_location_field() returns DAYS[fields.Date.today().weekday()] so 'today's location' is whichever day-of-week field matches the current weekday. _compute_exceptional_location_id searches hr.employee.location for rows with date == today and exposes them as exceptional_location_id (a non-stored compute, field-gated to hr.group_hr_user). Everywhere the effective location is read it is `exceptional_location_id or employee[dayfield]` (see _compute_presence_icon, _compute_work_location_name, _compute_work_location_type) — the dated exception always wins over the weekly default. None of this precedence is visible from field metadata; the fields look like 8 unrelated m2o.

behavioral_notes.element: hr.employee.get_views — the 'today's location' groupby/list hack (override of get_views)
behavioral_notes.observation: Because today's location lives in a different physical column every weekday, hr.employee overrides get_views(): after super(), it computes dayfield = _get_current_day_location_field() and string-replaces the placeholder field name 'today_location_name' with that real day field in the returned search-view arch, and replaces 'work_location_name' with it in the list-view arch, then injects the day field's definition into res['models'][self._name]['fields'] via fields_get([dayfield]). The XML views (views/hr_employee_views.xml) only ever reference the placeholder; the server rewrites the arch at fetch time so users can group/sort employees by 'where they work today'. This view-time arch rewrite is pure Python and invisible to static view/metadata extraction.

hr_homeworking re-paints the standard HR presence signal with the work-location type. hr.employee._compute_presence_icon extends @api.depends(*DAYS,'exceptional_location_id'), calls super(), then for the effective today location sets hr_icon_display = f'presence_{location_type}' (presence_home/presence_office/presence_other, the Selection values added via selection_add) and forces show_hr_icon_display=True. In parallel res.users._compute_im_status and res.partner._compute_im_status call super() and, when today's location has a location_type, rewrite the discuss IM status string to '<location_type>_<im_status>' (e.g. home_online, office_away) only for the online/away/busy/offline base states. So a single hr.employee.location row or weekday field silently changes both the kanban presence icon AND the chat presence badge of the linked partner — a multi-model side-effect no field/metadata layer reveals.

Deleting a hr.work.location is guarded by @api.ondelete(at_uninstall=False): _unlink_except_used_by_employee search_counts hr.employee for any of the 7 DAYS fields pointing at the location and raises UserError('You cannot delete locations that are being used by your employees') if so, then unlinks every hr.employee.location exception referencing it (so dated exceptions are cleaned but recurring assignments block the delete). Separately res.users declares the 7 location fields as related='employee_id.<day>_location_id' readonly=False and adds DAYS to _get_employee_fields_to_sync() plus the SELF_READABLE_FIELDS/SELF_WRITEABLE_FIELDS property lists — so a user editing their own weekly schedule on the user form writes straight through to their hr.employee record, and the calendar add-on's 'weekly' wizard branch relies on writing user_id.<day>_location_id. These guard/sync semantics are entirely behavioral.

Bundles: web.assets_backend, web.assets_unit_tests. None of this OWL behaviour is reachable from Python metadata.

capabilities: Define a recurring weekly work-location schedule per employee (Monday..Sunday: home/office/other)
Record dated exceptions to that schedule (one work location per employee per day)
Resolve and display where an employee works today (exception overrides weekly default)
Surface work location as a presence icon and a Discuss IM-status badge
Let an employee self-manage their own weekly schedule from the user preferences (self-readable/writeable)
Protect work-location master data from deletion while it is in use
value_streams: Set-Schedule-to-Presence: employee/HR sets weekly day fields (or a dated hr.employee.location exception) -> _compute_exceptional_location_id -> _compute_presence_icon / _compute_im_status -> colleagues see today's location on the kanban + chat
Group-by-Today's-Location: HR opens the employee list/search -> get_views swaps in the live day field -> employees grouped/filtered by where they work today
information_concepts: Weekly default work location (7 day-of-week fields on hr.employee/res.users/hr.employee.public)
hr.work.location (the location master, with location_type home/office/other)
Employee presence / IM status (decorated by location)
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; reuses base.group_user for self-service and hr.group_hr_user for full access / exceptional_location_id visibility)
policies: One work location per employee per day (unique(employee_id, date) Constraint on hr.employee.location)
A dated exception always overrides the weekly default for that day (exceptional_location_id or employee[dayfield] everywhere)

classification.rationale: hr_homeworking is an HR workforce-administration add-on, not a business object of any value chain/shop/network — it owns exactly one small transactional model, hr.employee.location (7 fields, unique(employee_id,date)), and otherwise decorates hr.employee/hr.employee.public/hr.work.location/res.users/res.partner (0 routes, 2 ACL + 2 ir.rule, ~326 py LOC, auto_install=true, category Human Resources/Remote Work, application=false). Per Stabell & Fjeldstad it is a SUPPORT activity (it administers the workforce; it neither transforms inputs into a product, nor solves client problems, nor brokers a network) and per Porter a support activity of HR/firm infrastructure. APQC maps to 7.0 Develop and Manage Human Capital — specifically the 7.x 'manage employee information / time, attendance and workforce' space: the module captures and publishes where each employee works (remote/office/other) on a weekly schedule plus dated exceptions, and turns that into a presence/availability signal. It does not recruit (7.1), train (7.3) or run payroll/benefits (7.4), so it sits in the employee-information / workforce-management nuance of 7.0. 8.0 Manage IT was rejected (it ships no IT-service plumbing — it has no routes or external calls), and 9.x/13.x were rejected (it manages people, not assets or generic capabilities).

standard_capabilities: Weekly per-employee work-location schedule (7 day-of-week home/office/other fields on hr.employee and res.users)
Dated work-location exceptions via hr.employee.location (one per employee per day)
Today's-location resolution (exception overrides weekly default) used by presence + IM status
Presence-icon + Discuss IM-status decoration by work location (home/office/other)
Self-service: an employee edits their own weekly schedule from user preferences
Group/filter employees by where they work today (get_views placeholder swap)
Deletion guard on hr.work.location while it is referenced by a schedule
typical_fits: Hybrid/remote teams publishing who is in the office vs at home each day
Showing colleague work location inline in Discuss/HR kanban presence
Employees self-managing their recurring remote days without HR intervention
common_gaps: Only a single location per employee per day (unique constraint) — no part-day / multi-location modelling
Weekly schedule is 7 fixed fields, not a date-ranged recurring rule — long-term plan changes need manual field edits or per-date exceptions
No approval workflow on remote days (a user can self-set their own schedule under base.group_user)
Calendar visualisation of the schedule requires the separate hr_homeworking_calendar add-on
No reporting/analytics on office occupancy beyond a today's-location groupby
